ideas.title: My first motor boat, on water that moves
ideas.critique: Round 1's boat had two weak points: the hand-made buoyancy and drag against still water. This version replaces both with a live height field and a buoyancy integral over the mesh, and that answers the earlier objection: the curve under a leaning friend can now really come out of the trim, and the same code floats anything. But much of its novelty is waves that rock and carry things, which is an example the human's goals already name. A shallow-water grid also has to resolve the paddles' wake at the scale of a single blade, or the 'local water velocity' turns into a fitted smear.

ideas.title: A lift up the cairn that brakes itself on the way down
ideas.critique: This is round 1's cairn hauler reworded, with the glowing wire swapped for friends who choose to ride. That fixes the 'excuse, not play' complaint: the load is the family, and the player has a real puzzle in gears, cells and counterweights. The braking that falls out of the circuit, with no brake code, is the strong part. The weak part is friends queueing and climbing in under their own locomotion: if they pop into the basket, the scene reads as staged.

ideas.title: A treadwheel the friends walk to make my current
ideas.critique: Friends as the power plant, with lamp load you can feel in their stride, is a charming link between creatures and the circuit. Torque as weight times offset is a one-axis rig, though, and a walk cycle on a moving rim that slips and tumbles is new animation work that easily slides back into a toy turning in place. The player's part is mostly flipping lamps on and off, and there is little to come back to after that.

ideas.title: The friends pull my first cart, then race it
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: It merges round 1's tug of war with the wheel on sand, and the merge answers the main objection to each: the cart actually moves, and it is no longer a machine left alone on the ground. It also builds the frame and wheels the big goal needs next, and showing what the motor is worth in friends is a payoff people will get. The risks are the ones already named: poses driven by the rope's force can fall back to sliding toys, and Bekker sinkage under a light wooden cart may show nothing.

ideas.title: Winding the coil by beak
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This is the first time the player's own handwork decides how well a part works: a rod laid on a turning rotor, with shorts found from what actually touches. That is honest and general, and it is the step the road calls for. As a watched result it is a weaker hum and a glow, close to the last two motor-and-wire posts, and the varnish wearing off where turns cross is likely to be a probability, not a mechanism.
